subsystems.name: Solar imaging payload
subsystems.role: images the corona to catch coronal mass ejections as they leave the Sun.

subsystems.name: In-situ solar wind sensors
subsystems.role: samples the plasma and magnetic field just before it reaches Earth.

subsystems.name: Spacecraft bus
subsystems.role: keeps the instruments pointed, powered and thermally stable in deep space.

subsystems.name: Communications and ground segment
subsystems.role: downlinks measurements and distributes them to forecasters.

subsystems.name: Orbit and station-keeping
subsystems.role: holds the spacecraft in a stable halo orbit at the Sun–Earth L1 or L5 point.

subsystems.name: Forecasting and alert system
subsystems.role: turns raw measurements into warnings for grid, aviation and satellite operators.

buildSteps.title: Choose the vantage points
buildSteps.detail: L1 sits about 1.5 million km sunward of Earth and gives roughly 30–60 minutes of warning before a solar wind stream arrives; L5 trails Earth by 60° and gives a side view of eruptions heading for Earth.

buildSteps.title: Design the instruments
buildSteps.detail: A coronagraph blocks the Sun's disk so faint coronal ejecta can be seen, while a magnetometer and plasma analyser measure the solar wind passing the spacecraft.

buildSteps.title: Build the spacecraft bus
buildSteps.detail: Structure, power, propulsion, thermal control and radiation-hard electronics are assembled and tested for deep-space operation.

buildSteps.title: Integrate and test
buildSteps.detail: Instruments are mounted, aligned and calibrated in thermal-vacuum chambers and vibration facilities before launch.

buildSteps.title: Launch and insert into orbit
buildSteps.detail: The spacecraft is launched to the L1 or L5 region and nudged into a halo orbit with small thruster burns.

buildSteps.title: Commission and calibrate
buildSteps.detail: Instruments are switched on, backgrounds measured and data products validated against existing monitors.

buildSteps.title: Operate in a constellation
buildSteps.detail: Data from multiple spacecraft are fused into forecast models, and replacement launches sustain continuous coverage.

prerequisites.tech: Deep-space launch and L1 halo-orbit operations
prerequisites.why: missions such as ACE, SOHO and DSCOVR have operated upstream of Earth for years.
eruptions must be detected near the Sun before their arrival can be predicted.

prerequisites.tech: In-situ solar wind plasma and field sensors
prerequisites.why: local measurements at L1 give the shortest-term warning of a coming shock.
a side-on vantage point improves eruption tracking, but no operational L5 monitor is yet in place.

prerequisites.tech: Coupling solar wind data to geomagnetic forecasts
prerequisites.why: predicting how a measured stream will disturb the magnetosphere remains uncertain.

pathway.milestone: L1 monitors such as ACE, SOHO and DSCOVR provide tens of minutes of warning for geomagnetic storms
pathway.unlocks: operators can put satellites into safe modes, reroute polar flights and prepare grids.

pathway.milestone: ESA's Vigil mission at L5 gives a side view of coronal mass ejections
pathway.unlocks: better eruption speed and arrival-time forecasts, extending warning by hours in some cases.

pathway.milestone: a multi-point constellation combining L1, L5, low-Earth-orbit sensors and ground magnetometers
pathway.unlocks: continuous, redundant coverage rather than reliance on a single ageing spacecraft.

pathway.milestone: automated feeds into grid, aviation and satellite operations
pathway.unlocks: faster protective actions and fewer false alarms.
